items.t: Wet and Wild Opener to Copa do Mundo da Vela 1/16 Finals
items.x:

items.html:
It was a very different Rio that greeted the arriving nations in the Copa do Mundo da Vela with the sunshine replaced by rain, and murky clouds hiding the the peak of Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer on Mount Corcovado.

The wind though was in, with 15 to 17 knots on Guanabara Bay, from the south-southwest.

Group A, Race 1 - Icebreakers Impress

It was a poor start in Group A for the defending champions, the Hungarian Shamans, starting behind as Ecuador started on the committee, Tahiti blitzing away from the pin, with Estonia in the middle.

The Estonian Icebreakers, so impressive in the 1/32 Finals, overhauled the Tahitian Black Pearls upwind, and the Shamans ground their way back into the game to round the top mark in second.

Downwind the fleet put the throttle down, showing impressive crewwork in the challenging conditions as white water rushed over the decks, hitting in excess of 17 knots at times. The grinders were pushed to the limit as the trimmers worked the spinnakers. This was sailing on the very edge of control.

While the grinders provided the brawn, the tacticians’ brains were similarly worked, connecting the windshifts as the rain clouds passed overhead. Every element of sailing skill was being tested.

The Icebreakers extended again, looking right at home in the conditions, while the Black Pearls closed on the Shamans upwind, rounding just 10 seconds behind at the final windward mark.

Estonia went on to win by a huge margin, while Hungary just held off Tahiti’s attack, and Ecuador have work to do to make an impact in this ultra-competitive group.

Icebreakers’ helm Mati Sepp was in good humour as he came ashore, “We were wondering: if we brought our Estonian weather - nasty and cold - we should sail well. So it was exactly like that.”

On how they sailed and the experience they gained in the 1/32 Finals Sepp added, “It was tricky. Many shifts, many puffs, so we tried to be conservative. We put in our best race with the crew work, and for sure those five days before are a big advantage, I'm sure.”

Group B, Race 1 - Ice Cool Chile Conquer the Monsoon

With the wind hitting 20 knots for Group B, Chile speared across the start line while Portugal forced Malaysia to tack off early as South Africa lagged at the back, looking ragged in the gusts.

The wind was up and down like a yo-yo, mainsails flogging in the gusts, down to just 10 knots in the lulls, making watching the wind an imperative.

There were problems about the South African Ubuntu yacht as the trim tab came off the keel, with the shore team quickly coming out to help, but putting them out of the race.

The Chilean team were excelling, closely followed by the Portuguese Navigators at the windward mark, but a monumental broach during their first gybe saw them briefly lose second to the Malaysian Monsoon team. The error clearly fired up the Navigators, hitting the afterburners to overhaul the Monsoon team in a wall of spray.

The charging Navigators continued their resurgence on the final upwind leg, closing right on the Chilean Finis Terrae team, powering past them to take the lead.

The two then match raced as the wind dropped up the course but, with the attention on each other, the Malaysian Monsoon team found great breeze on the right to jump into the lead.

Coming into the final windward mark it was anyone’s game in the shifts and gusts, with Malaysia tacking just beneath Portugal on the starboard layline with Chile just behind.

The teams were on tenterhooks hoisting their spinnakers, with Malaysia ahead as Chile shot past Portugal who had a slow hoist. Chile and Portugal gybed early as Malaysia fell out of the breeze on the right.

The big breeze on the left saw Chile power to the win, with Portugal once again deploying their submarine mode as water rushed over the deck to take second ahead of the unlucky Malaysia team.

A shivering Chilean helm Pedro Felipe Robles said on the dock after the race, “It's a very crazy and funny day, with a lot of wind gusts in different directions. All the trimmers are needed - always trimming the sails to catch that pressure, that puff, in the right direction.”

On their tactics he added, “We had a good start, leading the first upwind and the first downwind, and on the second upwind we probably made a few mistakes with the current, and that left us in third place, but in close contact with the leader. When we arrived at the windward mark, the wind went down, and we looked at the sea - a lot of wind puffs in different directions - and the tactician and the strategist made the best choice: an early gybe, to race on the left side of the course downwind. We caught the first puff, and with that puff we could build a lead for the whole downwind.”

Keeping control was at a premium downwind as Robles explained, “Helming is not easy, because the wind is not steady. There are holes with less wind and really aggressive puffs. Together with the trimmers we need to have a steady wheel and keep control of the spinnaker so we don't capsize.”

With the wind now topping 25 knots, the fleet were sent ashore and no more racing was possible for the day. While we only saw two races, the conditions made for thrilling racing.

Be sure to tune in on Friday on the @StarSailors YouTube channel with livestreams in six languages for the growing fanbase of the SSL Gold Cup, the Football World Cup in Sailing.

items.t: Tough Tests Ahead as Copa do Mundo da Vela 1/16 Finals Open
items.html:
Eight new national teams have arrived at the Axia Marina da Glória in Rio de Janeiro to compete in the SSL Gold Cup, the Football World Cup in Sailing. Each week the higher-ranked teams arrive, but those who have made it through the 1/32 Finals are practiced and know the race area. The challenge for the new teams is immense.

That said, the newly arrived nations boast some exceptional sailors. Olympians and World Champions are amongst their number, but how they work as a team will define their campaign. Individual talent is one thing, but the powerful SSL47 yachts require communication and harmony.

The Opening Ceremony was preceded by thunder and lightning, and the atmosphere will certainly be charged on the water on Thursday when the 1/16 Finals racing begins. The arriving teams were presented on stage and the winners of the SSL Snipe Challenge were lauded.

In Group A we have Estonia and Tahiti from the 1/32 Finals, taking on Ecuador and the might of Hungary - the defending SSL Gold Cup champions - led by the charismatic Zsombor Berecz. In Gran Canaria the Hungarian Shamans stunned the more established sailing nations, staging the most of dramatic of comebacks in the final, but nothing can be taken for granted with the well-drilled Estonian Icebreakers impressing and lightning-quick Tahiti in the last round, although they’ll be looking to reduce errors on the water. The fourth team are Equador, ranked #38 in the world and led by Julio Velez. This is going to be a tough group to progress from.

In Group B we have Chile, led by legendary captain Pablo Lorca, and Ian Ainslie’s South African team taking on qualifiers Portugal, with the exceptional afterguard of João Rodrigues and Afonso Domingos, and the Malaysian Monsoon team, captained by Khairulnizam Mohd Afendy, who were only a point behind Estonia in the 1/32 finals.

Noppakao Poonpat’s Thailand team and Eiichiro Hamazaki’s Japan will have it all to do in Group C as they face Rokas Milevičius and his Lithuanian team. They may have stuttered on the opening days of the 1/32 Finals, but they pulled it all together on Golden Sunday to progress, and we know from the inaugural SSL Gold Cup just how good they can be. Myanmar, the fourth nation in the group, were the story of the last round, snatching victory on the final leg to grasp their spot in the 1/16 Finals by the finest of margins.

Finally we have Group D, where Rodion Luka’s Ukraine team and the hugely impressive Uruguay team of 49er star Hernán Umpierre who qualified to face the Peruvian Paracas Warriors and the Czech Lakers captained by Ondřej Teplý. The higher-ranked, newly arrived teams will have to show their A-game from the off as this is one group you don’t want to have to stage a comeback in.

At this stage there are no easy groups. There is no clean passage to the 1/8 Finals. On Sunday we will be down to 24 teams still left in the competition, and every nation will want to be a part of that, especially with host nation Brazil entering the fray at that point.

SSL Snipe Challenge

The Axia Marina da Glória has been a hive of activity over the past three days, with more and more people coming to see the yachts in the marina, and visit the attractions, as well as 32 Snipe teams competing in the SSL Snipe Challenge, with the scoring inspired by the Copa do Mundo da Vela.

Tuesday saw the Qualifying Series, where all 32 dinghies raced together. Wednesday was Finals day, with a single Repecharge race for all those who finished between 11th and 32nd in the qualifiers battling for 2 places in the Quarter-Final.

These two teams then joined those boats which finished 3rd to 10th in the qualifiers, with the top five joining the team who finished 2nd in the qualifiers in the Semi-Final.

The top three then joined the qualifying series winner for the Final. A single race to decide the SSL Snipe Challenge winner.

Qualifying top on Tuesday proved to be of no advantage for Bruno Bethlem and Daniel Claro. Despite leading the race, they were penalised for excessive pumping downwind and went from first to last in the 4-boat race.

The USA’s Ernesto Rodriguez, reigning World Champion in the Snipe class, crewed by Argentina’s Diego Lipszyc, but they did it the hard way through qualifying in ninth place, and saved the best until last to win the Final and with it the title of SSL Snipe Challenge Champions.

“The qualifier was really tough for us. I mean it's a really tough fleet.”, said Ernesto. “The final was a good battle with Bruno and Juliana, and also Henrique on the last upwind leg. It was a really tight competition. We really enjoyed it to the last second.”

On not winning a race until the final, Ernesto added, “You're right about that. It's just a really tough fleet. I mean, the Brazilians are incredible. So yeah, we saved it the best for last, I guess. But I think we're a little fortunate. It was a smaller fleet as well, easier to control your competition. When you’ve got a big fleet with a lot of good sailors, it's really hard to pull out a win, so we're really fortunate that we barely made it to the finals, and then we found ourselves in a good position to win, and we did. We’re really, really happy about it.”

You can download photos from Photoshelter here. There will be live coverage on the @StarSailors YouTube channel every day.

items.t: 453 years of Niterói sailing history celebrated during Copa do Mundo da Vela
items.x: As the 1/32 Finals concluded on Sunday at the SSL Gold Cup, the Football World...
items.html:
As the 1/32 Finals concluded on Sunday at the SSL Gold Cup, the Football World Cup in Sailing, national team captains, dignitaries and officials from the SSL gathered at the Niterói Contemporary Art Museum (MAC), designed by Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer, with the fleet also parading past the Ilha da Boa Viagem, the historic, rocky island in Guanabara Bay connected to the island of Niterói.

Niterói has a long-standing sailing tradition, rooted in clubs such as Iate Clube Brasileiro, Rio Yacht Club, Clube Naval Charitas, Iate Clube Icaraí and Praia Clube São Francisco. Olympic medalists with strong ties to the city include Torben Grael, Lars Grael, Martine Grael, Marcelo Ferreira, Clínio de Freitas Neto and Isabel Marques Swan, who won bronze in the Women’s 470 class at the Beijing 2008 Olympics and currently serves as Niterói’s deputy mayor.

“Niterói is a city of sailors with a strong nautical tradition. We have around 40 outrigger canoe clubs, host major competitions and are home to great Olympic sailing medalists, including the Grael family. As an Olympic medalist and deputy mayor, it is an honor to welcome the SSL Gold Cup and pay tribute to Niterói on the city’s anniversary. This also highlights the importance of nautical sports to our local economy,” said Isabel Marques Swan.

During the Niterói celebrations, Isabel Marques Swan presented the SSL Gold Cup 2026 Niterói Trophy to the team that scored the highest score in the Round of 32. The award went to SSL Team Portugal, captained by seven-time Olympian João Rodrigues, who finished the round with an impressive total of 17 points.

The evening was accompanied by live music, with performances by: Federico Missio: tenor saxophone, Giulio Scaramella: piano, Rodrigo Villa: double bass, Julio Falavigna: drums.

The sailing calendar continues with the SSL Snipe Challenge scheduled for November 24–25 at AXIA Marina da Glória, followed by the Snipe Women’s Hemisphere Cup from November 26–29 at Clube Naval Charitas, in Niterói.

items.t: Heartbreak and Ecstasy in the Copa do Mundo da Vela
items.x: Golden Sunday in the 1/32 Finals . Eight teams progress in the Copa do Mundo da...
items.html:
Golden Sunday in the 1/32 Finals . Eight teams progress in the Copa do Mundo da Vela, while for eight it is heartbreak as they are eliminated. Sport can be cruel sometimes, but it is this emotion and drama that draws athletes to compete and test themselves against the best in the world.

On this golden day all races count for double points. Teams have worked out the numbers and know the result combinations which will see them qualify. While winning is foremost in their minds, those numbers are an ever-present thought for the captains and tacticians.

Group B, Race 4 - Ambers and Black Pearls shine in the Rio sun

With 14 knots of wind, sunshine, and a strong flood current, Guanabura Bay was playing its role perfectly. Going into the day, Greece had been deducted a point for failing to make their crew declaration - would this error prove costly?

Lithuania held beautifully on Greece’s hip on the left, and then found a high mode on port, climbing to Greece’s line into the windward mark to round first with Tahiti on their tail.

The Lithuanian Ambers and Tahiti Black Pearls powered downwind in unison as South Korea’s Red Fury and Greece’s Odysseus teams gybed early, trying to close the gap on the two leaders, but a poor drop by the Red Fury team saw them drop further back while Odysseus rounded over a minute behind.

Lithuania and Tahiti sat on Greece’s breeze upwind, knowing they had to finish above them to qualify, and in the process propelled South Korea back into third place at the final windward mark.

A twist in the spinnaker briefly caused consternation for the Black Pearls, but it popped out after a drop of the halyard, leading to a stunning parade of sail to the finish, framed by Sugarloaf Mountain.

Joy for Lithuania and Tahiti, anguish for Greece, who went into the

Lithuanian captain Rokas Milevičius was proud of his team, but knew they’d made life far from easy for themselves, “This is way more drama than I would like, I'm not going to lie. But I’m super proud of the team. It's not about myself - it's the whole bunch, we were improving each day. Even today I have three little points which I marked in my notes to improve. So I'm super happy with the performance of the team. It got a little bit risky, but you know, this is sailing. We executed our plan - we didn't want to get into the battle too early, because we knew that Greece was still in the game. So we executed as we wanted, and we feel very, very proud for Lithuania going to the next round.”

Tahiti Captain Teva Plichart had done the maths ahead of today to work out what they needed to do, “We took a few hours yesterday to understand what's going to happen if we do this, do that. We also had good news when we learned that Greece had a penalty. So when we took the start, we said, ‘OK, just be focused on the first two places’ and I did my best to take a good start and be safe, and we made it.”

Group C, Race 4 - Icebreakers cool under pressure as Monsoon storm to the win

A drag race left ensued in Group C as Seychelles started on the committee boat, Malaysia were bow forward beneath them, Cuba won the pin and Estonia were stuck between the two.

The Estonian Icebreakers gritted their teeth in the dirty air, tacking simultaneously with the Seychelles to find clear wind.

Coming into the windward mark, Cuba were furthest left, Malaysia were clear ahead and Estonia had climbed through the Seychelles.

Downwind the Icebreakers rose to second at the leeward gate, behind the Malaysian Monsoon team who had an ultra-conservative spinnaker drop. Meanwhile the Seychelles team struggled with their kite, falling back as they gathered it in.

Icebreakers’ helm Mati Sepp used his match racing experience to cover Cuba tack for tack upwind to cement their qualifying position, happy to leave the Monsoon team to take the race win.

The Malaysian team executed a perfect spinnaker hoist at the final windward mark to secure the race win as Estonia charged downwind on to their tail to win the group by a single point from Malaysia.

Estonian helm Mati Sepp was pleased how his team found the groove after a slow start, “It was the first time for us sailing with the medium in such strong winds, and we didn't have the proper trim at the start. So it took a couple of minutes until we found out, and it was too late already. But after that it was nice, we were always coming back.”

Malaysian Captain Khairulnizam Mohd Afendi summed up how the team felt after the race, “The team motivation was very high after the race - they gave all they have. We had two hard days before, and today they delivered very well. Credit to all the crew, I drive the boat like what I want to do, we executed the plan – so well done to them.”

Group D, Race 4 - Incredible last leg comeback for Inya

With Uruguay and Oman in the Group D box seats, Myanmar had it all to do and Singapore needed a miracle to qualify.

The Oman Lions of the Sea had the best start, followed by Uruguay’s La Celeste, with Singapore’s Guardians of the Bay tacking off early and Myanmar’s Inya team putting the squeeze on Uruguay after the tack, forcing La Celeste to tack back on to starboard.

The cream rose to the top at the windward mark with Uruguay rounding just inside Oman, while Singapore went head to wind to round a fraction behind, leading to the La Celeste team optimistically waving the

There was nothing to separate the leaders downwind with the two splitting choice of buoys at the leeward gate, but a knot in the halyard resulted in the Lions of the Sea relinquishing second place to Myanmar upwind, with the Inya team on the charge, closing right onto the tail of La Celeste, who tacked onto them, and the Inya team’s decision not to tack immediately cost them distance to the leaders.

On the final downwind leg the Myanmar team charged down the right, hitting 13 knots while Uruguay languished on the left, setting up a grandstand finish with qualification on the line. Against all odds, the Inya team surged again, crossing ahead of Uruguay and snatching the second qualification spot ahead of Oman in the most dramatic of circumstances alongside Uruguay.

Go back and watch the livestream to see just how incredible this comeback was. Sailing history in the making.

While Uruguay had the cards in their hands, Captain and helm Hernán Umpierre admitted it was far from straightforward today, “It really wasn't an easy race. We struggled a little bit with the boat speed upwind. We managed to find a really good lane on the first upwind, so we squeezed in there between Oman and Singapore. From there on we managed to keep the sailing quite simple. We are happy with the qualification, happy with the way we have been sailing these first days - I would say we are quite solid. We just need to take a look at some tactical moves and the gybes.”

The joy of Myanmar’s Captain Sithu Moe Myint was obvious, “It was unbelievable. It was a slim chance we came in with. Today wasn't like the last two days - there weren't a lot of opportunities, so we had to keep it tight, and we had to take one of the very few opportunities that were given to us. The team executed really well, and we're all ecstatic crossing that line first. It's about time - we've been in the lead in the first race and the third, and it's time that we secured this win. So we're ecstatic.”

Group A, Race 4 - Navigators plot their route to the 1/16 Finals

Antigua & Barbuda had it all to do in Group A, five points away from the top two teams, and went hard on the attack in the pre-start with both Portugal and Ukraine, but picked up a penalty in the process and ended up starting behind the pack.

The Portuguese Navigators, with the unflappable Afonso Domingos on the helm, emerged unscathed on the left, unfazed by the aggression, rounding the top mark comfortably ahead of the Colombian Golden Coffee Team with Ukraine’s United team on their tail, diving low on the spinnaker set to pile pressure on the Colombian team.

The misery continued for Antigua & Barbuda’s Rum Runners when their spinnaker drop stalled as the Navigators continued to extend at the front. There was nothing to separate Colombia and Ukraine, rounding the final windward mark nose to tail.

The Navigators went on to win at a canter, while Ukraine’s United team ground down the Colombian Golden Coffee yacht, taking second and qualifying alongside Portugal for the 1/16th finals.

Portuguese helm Afonso Domingos was pleased the team executed the plan without drama, ”It was fantastic. Everything ran as we were planning, so it was really great. All the crew did a fantastic job during these days, and to finish like that is really fantastic.”

Ukrainian Captain Rodion Luka was pleased to qualify, but was also enthralled to see how the level continues to increase in the SSL Gold Cup, “When I'm watching the races I say, ‘Wow, the teams are improving every day. They're making fewer and fewer technical mistakes.’ Like, you could see the team from Myanmar - they're qualifying, they're doing so well. Each team is getting better and better. Every hour makes a huge difference.”

The SSL family gathered at the main stage in AXIA Marina da Glória to celebrate the winners, as well as what has been an incredible way to open the Copa do Mundo da Vela.

So the nations qualified are now on the matchboard in the sailors’ lounge and it’s time for a well-earned rest for those teams, while the rest are on the plane home. Sport can be cruel but is also rewarding in equal measure.

items.t: Só acaba quando termina! Viradas derrubam favoritos e classificam Mianmar e Malásia na Copa do Mundo da Vela
items.x: GRÉCIA ENTRA NA ÚLTIMA REGATA COM A CLASSIFICAÇÃO ENCAMINHADA, MAS ACABA...
items.html:
Grécia entra na última regata com a classificação encaminhada, mas acaba eliminada; Portugal e Uruguai confirmam força na Baía de Guanabara, enquanto oito seleções avançam à próxima fase

Na SSL Gold Cup, a chamada Copa do Mundo da Vela, estar classificado no papel não significa ter a vaga garantida na água. A última rodada da fase de 1/32 do evento disputado, disputada neste domingo (22), na Baía de Guanabara, no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) mostrou como uma única regata pode mudar o destino de uma seleção. E principalmente quando essa prova tem pontuação dobrada.

A seleção Grécia viu na pratica a máxima do futebol de que o jogo só acaba quando termina. O time entrou virtualmente classificado e ficou de fora do top 2 no Grupo B. Os gregos dependiam de uma combinação considerada favorável, mas terminaram eliminados quando menos poderiam errar.

Lituânia e Taiti passaram de fase, com o país asiático ganhando de forma surpreendente a última regata da chave. Outras seleções do continente como Mianmar e Malásia aproveitaram a pontuação em dobro para conquistar classificações que pareciam distantes, enquanto Portugal, Estônia e Uruguai confirmaram o desempenho regalar das primeiras provas e vão ao round 1/16.

“Passamos algumas horas fazendo os cálculos para entender o que aconteceria em cada cenário. Quando soubemos que a Grécia havia recebido uma penalização, decidimos nos concentrar nas duas primeiras posições. Procurei fazer uma boa largada, sem correr riscos desnecessários, e conseguimos”, contou Teva Plichart, comandante do Taithi.

A matemática abriu espaço para reviravoltas, obrigando as tripulações a acompanhar não apenas a própria posição, mas também a dos adversários. Ao final, Portugal, Ucrânia, Taiti, Lituânia, Estônia, Malásia, Uruguai e Mianmar garantiram presença na fase de 1/16 de final, programada para começar na quinta-feira (26), na Marina da Glória, sede da segunda edição da SSL Gold Cup.

Além das oito equipes classificadas neste domingo, entram na competição Hungria, atual campeã da Copa do Mundo da Vela, Equador, Chile, África do Sul, Tailândia, Japão, Peru e República Tcheca.

As regatas que decidiram a fase 1/32

Com vento sul de aproximadamente 14 nós e sensação térmica superior a 40°C, a competição definiu os oito países que continuam na disputa pelo título mundial. Foram quatro regatas ao todo, uma para cada grupo, de até 40 minutos. Será assim até a final em 13 de dezembro.

O regulamento ajudou a transformar a última rodada em uma sequência de decisões. Nas três primeiras regatas, a vitória valia quatro pontos. Neste domingo, passou a valer oito, com seis para o segundo colocado, quatro para o terceiro e dois para o quarto.

A maior mudança aconteceu no Grupo B. A Grécia, conhecida como Odysseus, entrou na água com a liderança da chave e viu sua vantagem desaparecer ao terminar a regata na quarta colocação.

O Taiti, dos Black Pearls, comandado por Teva Plichart, venceu a disputa decisiva, enquanto a Lituânia, dos Ambers, liderada por Rokas Milevičius, terminou em segundo. A Coreia do Sul ficou em terceiro e também se despediu da competição.

A Lituânia também precisou administrar a pressão. O líder Rokas Milevičius explicou que a equipe evitou antecipar o confronto direto com a Grécia e encontrou na correnteza uma oportunidade para executar a estratégia.

“Foi muito mais drama do que eu gostaria. Estou muito orgulhoso da equipe, porque melhoramos a cada dia. Tínhamos um plano e conseguimos executá-lo. Identificamos uma linha de correnteza e procuramos tirar a Grécia daquela região. Foi essa separação que buscamos”, afirmou o comandante lituano.

Mianmar vence na hora certa e Malásia completa recuperação

No Grupo D, o Uruguai, chamado de La Celeste, confirmou a primeira colocação com 17 pontos, mas a disputa pela segunda vaga teve uma definição apertada. Mianmar, conhecido como Inya, precisava vencer a regata decisiva e conseguiu superar os uruguaios na reta final. Com o resultado, chegou aos mesmos 14 pontos de Omã, os Lions of the Sea, mas levou a classificação pelo critério de desempate, graças ao melhor resultado na última prova.

“Foi inacreditável. Chegamos com uma chance pequena e sabíamos que não teríamos muitas oportunidades. Precisávamos aproveitar uma das poucas que aparecessem. A equipe executou tudo muito bem e cruzar a linha de chegada em primeiro foi uma emoção enorme”, disse Sithu Moe Myint, comandante de Mianmar.

O Uruguai terminou a fase com três resultados entre os dois primeiros colocados e nove regatas acumuladas desde a seletiva pan-americana, realizada também no Rio de Janeiro. A experiência pode pesar na sequência da competição, quando novas seleções entrarão diretamente na disputa.

“As equipes que entram agora treinaram aqui em outubro, então não chegam sem conhecer o barco. Mas ter nove regatas de competição certamente ajuda. É uma vantagem que vamos tentar usar a nosso favor. Cada grupo fica mais difícil, e precisamos continuar melhorando”, acrescentou o uruguaio Fernando Taboada.

No Grupo C, a Malásia, chamada de Monsoon, protagonizou outra recuperação. Depois de enfrentar dificuldades nas duas primeiras regatas, a equipe comandada por Khairulnizam Mohd Afendi venceu a prova decisiva e terminou com 16 pontos, garantindo a segunda vaga. A Estônia, dos Icebreakers, avançou na liderança, com 17 pontos, enquanto Cuba e Seychelles foram eliminadas.

“Os dois primeiros dias foram difíceis, mas ontem e hoje a tripulação entregou tudo. Eles deram o melhor que tinham. Revemos os vídeos diariamente, identificamos os pontos que precisamos melhorar e hoje conseguimos dar mais um passo. Estou muito orgulhoso da equipe”, declarou Khairulnizam Mohd Afendi.

A Estônia, por sua vez, soube administrar a vantagem construída anteriormente. “Estava muito claro para nós. Não estávamos preocupados com a Malásia. Nosso objetivo era marcar Cuba e garantir a posição”, afirmou o skipper Mati Sepp .

Portugal domina grupo e Ucrânia acompanha

No Grupo A, Portugal, os Navegadores, encerrou a primeira fase com 19 pontos e a melhor campanha entre as 16 seleções que disputaram esta etapa. A equipe venceu a última regata e confirmou a liderança da chave, seguida pela Ucrânia, os Haydamaky, com 16 pontos. Colômbia e Antígua e Barbuda ficaram pelo caminho. Os lusitanos já entraram classificados.

“Tudo aconteceu como planejamos. A tripulação fez um trabalho muito bom durante esses dias, e terminar dessa maneira foi excelente”, avaliou o português Afonso Domingos, comandante do time.

Comandante da Ucrânia, o medalhista olímpico Rodion Luka observou que o nível das disputas vem aumentando a cada dia. “As equipes estão melhorando continuamente e cometendo cada vez menos erros técnicos. Basta olhar para Mianmar, que conseguiu a classificação, e para Omã, que também evoluiu muito. Cada hora de navegação faz uma diferença enorme”.

Entre os eliminados, a Colômbia, dos Golden Coffee, encerrou sua participação com o terceiro lugar na última regata. Esteban Echavarría, que integra a equipe ao lado de Juan Esteban Restrepo, destacou a experiência no Rio de Janeiro e o impacto da competição sobre a vela colombiana.

“Foi um dia espetacular. Conseguimos sair da quarta para a terceira posição, mas não foi suficiente para classificar. Estamos satisfeitos com nosso desempenho. O Rio nos recebeu de braços abertos, e toda a comunidade da vela na Colômbia acompanhou as transmissões. Isso inspira não apenas quem está na SSL, mas também os atletas das classes olímpicas e amadoras”, afirmou Esteban Echavarría, que continuará no Brasil para disputar o SSL Snipe Challenge.

Cuba, os Pirates of the Caribbean, também encerrou a campanha depois de conquistar uma das vagas na seletiva pan-americana. “Foram regatas muito intensas, bonitas e divertidas. A equipe cubana entregou tudo até o último momento. Entramos hoje com chances de avançar e não conseguimos, mas saímos satisfeitos com o desenvolvimento do time e com a certeza de que lutamos até o fim”, declarou Darien Martínez Pimentel.

Niterói comemora aniversário com homenagem aos velejadores

A rodada decisiva também marcou os 453 anos de Niterói (RJ), celebrados neste domingo (22). Em homenagem à cidade, o percurso das regatas passou pelas proximidades da Ilha da Boa Viagem, e os capitães das seleções participaram de uma cerimônia no Museu de Arte Contemporânea de Niterói (MAC), projetado por Oscar Niemeyer.

A cidade tem uma ligação histórica com a vela, construída em clubes como o Iate Clube Brasileiro, o Rio Yacht Club (Sailing), o Clube Naval Charitas, o Iate Clube Icaraí e o Praia Clube São Francisco. Entre os medalhistas olímpicos ligados ao município estão Torben Grael, Lars Grael, Martine Grael, Marcelo Ferreira, Clínio de Freitas Neto e Isabel Marques Swan, bronze na classe 470 nos Jogos de Pequim 2008 e atual vice-prefeita de Niterói.

“Niterói é uma cidade de velejadores e tem uma vocação náutica muito forte. Temos cerca de 40 clubes de canoa havaiana, recebemos competições importantes e somos a cidade de grandes medalhistas olímpicos da vela, como a família Grael. É uma honra, como medalhista olímpica e vice-prefeita, receber a SSL Gold Cup e homenagear Niterói justamente no aniversário da cidade. Isso também mostra a força dos esportes náuticos para a nossa economia”, afirmou Isabel Marques Swan.

A programação na cidade carinhosamente chamada de Nikiti segue com o SSL Snipe Challenge, nos dias 24 e 25 de novembro, na Marina da Glória, e a Snipe Women's Hemisphere Cup, de 26 a 29 de novembro, no Clube Naval Charitas, em Niterói.

Como funciona a Copa do Mundo da Vela

A SSL Gold Cup 2026 reúne 40 seleções nacionais em uma competição disputada em barcos idênticos da classe SSL47, com aproximadamente 14 metros de comprimento. As equipes são formadas por velejadores de diferentes classes, incluindo medalhistas olímpicos, campeões mundiais e profissionais com experiência nas principais competições internacionais.

O formato é inspirado na Copa do Mundo de futebol, com seleções divididas em grupos de quatro países. As duas melhores equipes de cada grupo avançam à fase seguinte, enquanto as demais são eliminadas. As seleções mais bem posicionadas no ranking mundial da Star Sailors League entram diretamente nas etapas posteriores. A decisão do título será disputada em uma única regata entre quatro finalistas, no dia 13 de dezembro.

Sobre a Star Sailors League (SSL)

A Star Sailors League (SSL) é uma organização internacional de vela criada para promover competições entre velejadores de diferentes classes e nacionalidades. A entidade desenvolveu a SSL Gold Cup, conhecida como Copa do Mundo da Vela, competição por equipes nacionais que reúne atletas de diferentes gerações e modalidades da vela. A SSL também mantém um ranking internacional de velejadores, utilizado como referência para a participação das seleções na competição.
